subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and established component-API practice (compound components, slots, render props, headless primitives, asChild, configuration-vs-composition).

cases.scenario: A Card component has accumulated 14 boolean props (hasHeader, hasFooter, isCompact, showAction, isElevated, ...) and a new request needs yet another variant the props don't cover.
cases.context: The card is reused across many surfaces and the team keeps editing the shared component for each new variant.
cases.question: How should the agent redesign the Card API?
expected_flags: Move to a composition API (Card with Card.Header / Card.Body / Card.Footer, or named slots)
Reduce boolean props to single digits; let consumers compose unanticipated variants
Distinguish module-identity variants (prop) from consumer-usage variants (slot)
Optionally keep a high-level convenience component over the composable primitives
expected_fix_hints: Expose slots/children so the new variant needs no edit to the shared component
Refactor the prop set into compound children sharing context
absent_signals: Do not add another boolean prop for the new variant
Do not keep editing the shared component for every consumer's case

cases.scenario: A Dialog is implemented as a single component with title, body, and closeLabel string props; a consumer needs the close button to be a custom icon button and the title to contain a badge.
cases.context: The team wants consumers to control the trigger, content, and close affordance.
cases.question: What composition design should the agent recommend?
expected_flags: Use a compound-component API: Dialog.Trigger, Dialog.Content, Dialog.Close as addressable parts sharing context
Children require the parent's context (render outside the parent only with an explicit error)
Use asChild so Dialog.Trigger/Close can wrap a custom element while inheriting behavior and ARIA
Keep accessibility wiring (focus return on close, aria attributes) the module's responsibility
expected_fix_hints: Expose Dialog.Trigger / Dialog.Content / Dialog.Close instead of string/prop config
Apply asChild to delegate markup while preserving behavior
absent_signals: Do not keep string props for the title/close affordance
Do not push focus/ARIA responsibility onto the consumer

cases.scenario: A Table component bakes in markup and styles, and the team now needs a second, visually different table reusing the same sorting/selection/pagination behavior.
cases.context: State, behavior, and presentation are currently conflated in one component.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the module?
expected_flags: Extract a headless primitive: expose state and behavior (sorting, selection, pagination) as hooks/unstyled components
Separate the three conflated concerns — state, behavior, presentation
Let each visual treatment be a consumer of the headless behavior, with its own markup/styles
Adding a second visual treatment becomes trivial once behavior is separated
expected_fix_hints: Provide a useTable / headless table primitive that returns state + handlers
Build both visual tables on top of the shared headless layer
absent_signals: Do not fork the whole component to make a second visual style
Do not duplicate the sorting/selection logic per visual variant

cases.scenario: A Tooltip.Trigger always renders its own <button>, so wrapping an existing <Button> produces a button nested inside a button and broken focus behavior.
cases.context: The consumer wants the existing Button to be the trigger without an extra wrapper element.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the trigger API?
expected_flags: Use the asChild / polymorphic pattern so the trigger renders the consumer's element instead of its own
This collapses the two-level wrapper and avoids the button-inside-button accessibility error
The parent must clone or render-prop its single child carefully to merge props/behavior
All behavior and ARIA wiring must be preserved across the element swap
expected_fix_hints: Add asChild support to Tooltip.Trigger and merge behavior onto the passed child
Forward refs and ARIA attributes onto the consumer's element
absent_signals: Do not keep rendering an extra wrapper button
Do not drop ARIA/focus behavior when delegating the element

cases.scenario: A developer wants to build a one-off settings panel that appears in exactly one screen as a full compound-component system with slots, context, and headless hooks.
cases.context: The panel is single-use within one feature and there is no plan to reuse it.
cases.question: How should the agent respond to the proposed design?
expected_flags: Composition machinery is overkill for a single-use, never-reused component
Reach for the simpler prop-driven shape instead
Compound/headless patterns earn their cost through reuse and unanticipated variants, absent here
Recommend the simplest API that works for the one use
expected_fix_hints: Build a plain prop-driven panel; revisit composition only if reuse emerges
Avoid context/slots/headless hooks for a one-screen component
absent_signals: Do not build a full compound-component system for a single-use panel
Do not add headless hooks where there is no second consumer

cases.scenario: A PM asks the design-module-composition owner to pick the brand font for headings and decide the card border-radius value.
cases.context: The team conflates 'component design' with all visual-token decisions.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Font and border-radius are out of scope — those are visual styling / design tokens
Redirect to visual-design-foundations / layout-composition for visual decisions
This skill owns the module's composition API shape, not its visual values
Correctly redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand visual-token choices to visual-design-foundations / layout-composition
Offer the in-scope part: how the component exposes styling hooks/slots to consumers
absent_signals: Do not pick the brand font
Do not choose the border-radius value

cases.scenario: A team asks how to version, publish, and configure the shared component library package that hosts these modules.
cases.context: The question is about the library's packaging and release, not any single module's API.
cases.question: How should the agent scope this request?
expected_flags: Publishing/versioning the shared library is out of scope — that is design-system-architecture
This skill owns the composition API of an individual module, not the library's packaging
Redirect the packaging/release concern to design-system-architecture
Correctly distinguishes module API shape from library lifecycle
expected_fix_hints: Stay on module-level composition API questions
absent_signals: Do not design the package release/versioning here
Do not conflate one module's API with the library's distribution
